title: Sui Dynasty
summary: Yang Jian, later Emperor Wendi, took power in 581 and conquered the south by 589, ending about three centuries of division. In under four decades and two reigns, the Sui centralised government, issued a single law code, extended the equal-field land system, chose officials by civil service examination, and dug the Grand Canal linking the Yellow and Yangtze rivers. Costly wars in Korea fed revolts that ended the dynasty in 618, and the Tang built on its reforms.

uncertainty.note: Reunification of the south was completed in 589 with the conquest of the Chen dynasty.

where.modern_name: Xi'an, Shaanxi, China (stand-in pin for the Sui imperial capital Daxing/Chang'an)

importance.justification: Reunified China after three centuries of division and laid the institutions the Tang inherited (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: The Grand Canal was expanded and unified under the Sui dynasty to link northern and southern agricultural and economic centers.
The imperial civil service examination system had its beginnings under the Sui dynasty to select officials on merit.

reviewer_note: Coordinator review 2026-11-12: summary rewritten to claims on src-whe-sui and src-afe-columbia ("more than three centuries" changed to the source wording; reunification dated 581-589). Pin at Daxing/Chang an, named capital on both sources; Luoyang and Jiangdu were also capitals.
